Asked for color on the process of adding DSD partners (now 135+), which retailers flip to DSD in H2 and the impact, and inventory/production capacity; plus H2 retailer resets/SKU additions and marketing plans.

At ~135 DSD partners covering ~70% of major NA metro markets, gaps targeted in Q3. Target green-lighted to convert route-to-market late Aug into Sep; CDS majority converts H2; Walmart ~January 2021. Increased inventories from Q1 to ensure supply, with a new Southeast co-packer test run next week. Peach Vibe demand required a quick production restart; delayed resets push the flavor into more accounts in H2 and 2021.
Asked whether Celsius needs to react as competitors (Red Bull, Monster) ramp promotions during COVID; and for a current/forward DSD penetration percentage and how the DSD partner strategy evolves.

Category always promotional; Celsius participated in targeted programs (July 7-Eleven BOGO, Target, CDS) but will not discount extensively — maintaining margins, driving premiumization. DSD penetration ~10-12% last quarter, now 'in the teens,' expected to grow each quarter as big retailers (CDS, Target, Walmart, Rite Aid, 7-Eleven) transition; partner count (135) will grow further.
Asked about channel performance — gas/convenience, online, gyms — and trajectory through Q2; Celsius's demographic vs. competitors; and July vs. June heading into the seasonally strongest quarter.

Fitness channel significantly impaired (gyms at 25-50% capacity) but offset by Amazon/mass/grocery growth. Gas/convenience ~11-12.5% ACV growing ~50%, with Circle K, QT, RaceTrac and 7-Eleven additions. ~50/50 male/female split, aged-up consumer (45-50). Reiterated North America purchase orders over 50% above prior year, setting up a strong 2021.
Asked Celsius's Amazon channel YoY growth rate; how COVID-19 has changed day-to-day team practices; and whether COVID-related sanitation expenses are material.

Celsius growing well above the Amazon category's ~88% rate — citing ~180% growth — gained 1 share point as Red Bull lost 1, putting Celsius close to #2. Teams working remotely with contingency plans, missing in-person customer touch points during the 2021 buyer season. CFO said COVID sanitation expenses not material; CEO added the larger cost is an opportunity cost from limited new-distributor activation and delayed retailer resets.

Asked how new distribution agreements help with shelf placement and cooler/checkout positioning; and how Celsius views the evolving competitive landscape — whether it is a 'rising tide lifts all boats' dynamic.

DSD distributors function as brand ambassadors — 'faces sell cases; and when it's cold, it's sold' — providing manpower to educate, merchandise and build share. Beverages have low barriers to entry but high barriers to succeed; Celsius's focus is brand equity and distribution to take share in an inherently competitive category.
